quick.summary: Why your bills are high and how separating parts helps.
quick.takeaway: Store data cheaply, and only pay for power when running reports.

beats.line: Our database bills doubled, but we barely added new users. Why?
Imagine buying a new house just to park a second car.
That is crazy. I just need a bigger garage.
Exactly. But your current setup glues the house and garage together.
When you need data space, you buy processing power too.
We call this tightly coupled architecture.
Can I just say glued together? Coupled sounds romantic.
Glued together it is. Unglue the space from the power.
So we store data cheaply, and only pay for power to run reports.
Right. Buy the big garage, but only rent the fast car.

quiz.question: Why is separating data storage from processing power a good choice?
options: You can scale space without paying for power you do not need.
It makes the code run faster by default.
It removes the need for database backups.
It forces the team to write better queries.
quiz.explanation: Separation allows you to buy cheap storage for data, and only pay for compute power when actively processing it.

quiz.question: A glued together architecture allows you to upgrade storage independently from processing.
quiz.explanation: If it is glued together, increasing storage forces you to buy more processing power as well.
